messages:
anna_cs: Horizon flagged auth failures after key rotation. can we triage? looks like traffic dropped and some requests 401/403.

horizon-eng: yes — most calls from our app show 401 Unauthorized, a few 403 with body: {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"missing:chat.write"}. we rotated keys via the console and redeployed. nothing else changed.

dev_jun: two quick checks: 1) are you actually reading the new env var in your container? 2) did the key get the expected scopes (chat, embeddings)?

horizon-eng: deployment uses env name REDWOOD_API (we set REDWOOD_API_KEY when creating secret). our app reads process.env.REDWOOD_API so it was still hitting old/empty value. oops.

leo_devx: yep that would produce 401 (no auth header) or 403-like scope errors if a fallback token is present. can you show the k8s manifest snippet?

horizon-eng: snippet: 
```yaml
env:
  - name: REDWOOD_API
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: horizon-redwood
        key: key
```

dev_jun: fix: change name to REDWOOD_API_KEY or update app to read REDWOOD_API. easy rollout. also double-check secret contents match the UI token.

horizon-eng: updated manifest to REDWOOD_API_KEY and applied, restarted pods. auths look better but we saw a short window of 429s as all pods restarted at once and reconnected.

anna_cs: noted — bulk restarts can cause client-side connection bursts. recommend rolling restart strategy (maxUnavailable:1) or use a staged rollout.

leo_devx: also adding a small client-side guard: SDK should detect missing key env and log a clear onboarding hint (masked) so this is easier to spot. low-risk patch: `if (!key) console.warn('REDWOOD_API_KEY missing — see quickstart')`. will do.

onboard-bot: ticket CS-2301 created: SDK add missing-key warning + docs checklist add env var name note and restart guidance.

horizon-eng: thanks all — fixed on our side and no further errors. leaving this thread closed unless regressions appear. :slightly_smiling_face:
